metadata.title: R3 beam fall · V1 / V2 causal boards
metadata.description: At approximately 1:03 PM on October 14, 2024 (Turn 2), the R3 Exit Carrier Beam at the Indiana Harbor 80-inch Hot Strip roughing mill fell from the yoke into the R3 mill pit, landing on the sled and a scaffold platform. No team members were in the pit at the time, though several contractor employees had worked in the pit throughout the morning, and two contractor employees walking beside the mill stand witnessed the fall. The area was red-flagged for investigation. The beam and its link were found intact with the keeper still installed; no damage was apparent on the yoke on which the link rests. A small mill window liner from the top operator side fell with the beam. No crane lifts involving this equipment were in progress or had occurred prior. On the previous shift, the work rolls and top and bottom backup rolls had been removed in preparation for outage work in the mill stand; the R3 top backup roll balance had been left isolated in the raised position, and the B hydraulics had been shut off and bled for work on that system.
metadata.note: Saved Qwen V1 and V2 from the R3 follow-up run. These are historical model outputs, not a verified or completed RCA. V3 and V4 remain in the original investigation.

nodes.label: R3 exit carrier beam falls from yoke into mill pit
nodes.detail: Beam and link landed on sled/scaffold platform at ~1:03 PM.

nodes.label: Relative movement cleared interference point (link-arm stop)
nodes.detail: Yoke moved downward; beam displaced off-center, clearing the yoke/lifting point.

nodes.label: Top backup roll balance exerts gravity load on carrier beam/link
nodes.detail: Balance remained in raised position after hydraulics bled (0 psi). No independent mechanical restraint documented.

nodes.label: Keeper device failed to retain link arm against gravity after displacement
nodes.detail: Beam fell despite keeper being installed. Sufficiency under off-center load is unverified.

nodes.label: Blank field for mechanical block ID in LOTO record (R3-EV-005)
nodes.detail: No independent verifier signature or physical restraint documented for gravity control.

nodes.label: Assumption that hydraulic isolation/wedging suffices for gravity control without block
nodes.detail: Hydraulics bled; reliance on 'wedged' state rather than positive mechanical restraint.

nodes.label: System design lacks carrier-beam stop to prevent wedging on spreader/posts when backup rolls absent
nodes.detail: Off-center displacement possible; no inherent mechanical feature prevents clearance of lifting point.

nodes.label: Anonymous handwritten turnover note lacks chain of custody/verification
nodes.detail: Note regarding keeper inspection exists but is not authoritative evidence of verification.

edges.rationale: Assuming wedging sufficed led to failure to install/verify mechanical block, leaving barrier dependent on unreliable condition.
edges.counterfactual: If a verified mechanical block had been installed and documented before bleeding hydraulics, the gravity load would have been arrested regardless of wedging loss.
edges.evidenceGap: Engineering analysis of Keeper rating vs. off-center displacement.

edges.rationale: Blank LOTO field indicates failure to secure gravity load with independent restraint.
edges.counterfactual: If a mechanical block ID had been recorded and verified, the barrier would have existed independently of hydraulic pressure or wedging.
edges.competingExplanation: Block was physically present but undocumented (unverified).

edges.rationale: Lack of inherent stop allowed beam to displace off-center when yoke moved, clearing the lifting point.
edges.counterfactual: If a mechanical stop existed on the carrier beam or yoke pocket, displacement would not have cleared the interference point.
edges.competingExplanation: Stop exists but was bypassed by operator error (unverified).
edges.evidenceGap: Mechanical design drawings for R3 stand.

edges.rationale: Once interference point cleared, gravity load on raised balance caused beam to fall.
edges.counterfactual: If barrier (block or verified keeper) had remained effective after displacement, the event would not have occurred.
edges.evidenceGap: Operational logs contradict crane claim; witness testimony supports no crane.

edges.rationale: Reliance on unverified handwritten note instead of formal verification contributed to barrier failure.
edges.counterfactual: If a competent authority had verified and documented the keeper check before Turn 2 work, the event might have been prevented or detected earlier.

verificationFindings.issue: Causal edge relies on unsupported design claim and unverified bypass hypothesis.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Mechanical design drawings for R3 stand to confirm absence of carrier-beam stop; physical inspection or witness testimony regarding whether a stop existed but was bypassed.
verificationFindings.question: Does the mechanical design drawing for R3 show an inherent stop preventing off-center displacement? If yes, provide evidence that it was present and functional during the event interval.

verificationFindings.issue: Causal edge attributes failure to an unverified handwritten note rather than documented procedure or physical verification.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Turnover log R3-EV-006 and any associated witness statements regarding the specific keeper check performed before Turn 2 work; evidence of who verified what and when.
verificationFindings.question: Was there a formal, signed verification record for the keeper installation prior to bleeding hydraulics? If not, why was reliance placed on an anonymous handwritten note?

verificationFindings.issue: Causal edge assumes wedging sufficed as a barrier condition without evidence of its reliability or rating.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Engineering analysis comparing Keeper rating to off-center displacement forces; inspection logs confirming whether the beam was actually wedged at the time hydraulics were bled.
verificationFindings.question: Was there an engineering assessment establishing that 'wedging' provided a reliable barrier against gravity load? If not, why was this assumption accepted as sufficient?

verificationFindings.issue: Causal edge links blank LOTO field to failure without confirming whether a physical block existed but went undocumented.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Physical inspection log R3-EV-017 or equivalent contemporaneous record showing actual presence/absence of mechanical restraint at the time hydraulics were bled.
verificationFindings.question: Did a mechanical block physically exist on the gravity control point when hydraulics were isolated? If yes, why was it not recorded in the LOTO field?

verificationFindings.issue: Node status is 'unknown' because sufficiency of keeper under off-center load has never been verified.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Engineering analysis or test data showing Keeper capacity relative to expected displacement forces; physical inspection confirming whether the beam was wedged at failure time.
verificationFindings.question: Was there an engineering evaluation determining that the installed keeper could withstand the specific off-center loading conditions present during this event?

nodes.label: Focal Event: R3 Exit Carrier Beam Falls
nodes.detail: Beam and link landed on sled/scaffold platform at ~1:03 PM. No injuries reported.

nodes.label: Condition: Gravity Load Unrestrained (Hydraulics Bled)
nodes.detail: Top backup roll balance left in raised position with hydraulics isolated and bled (0 psi). No documented independent positive mechanical control.

nodes.label: Condition: Design Lacks Inherent Stop for Off-Center Displacement
nodes.detail: System design lacks carrier-beam stop to prevent wedging on mill spreader/posts when backup rolls absent.

nodes.label: Condition: Procedure Gap (No Independent Restraint Requirement Confirmed)
nodes.detail: Blank field for mechanical block ID in LOTO record; requirement for independent restraint when hydraulics bled is not explicitly confirmed.

nodes.label: Condition: Procedure Gap (No Formal Keeper Verification)
nodes.detail: Anonymous handwritten turnover note regarding keeper inspection lacks chain of custody and formal verification.

nodes.label: Event: Off-Center Displacement Clears Interference Point
nodes.detail: Yoke moved downward; beam displaced off-center, clearing the yoke/lifting point.

nodes.label: Event: Gravity Load Causes Fall After Clearance
nodes.detail: Once interference point cleared, gravity load on raised balance caused beam to fall.

nodes.label: Barrier: Reliance on Wedged State (Unverified)
nodes.detail: Assumption that hydraulic isolation/wedging sufficed for gravity control without block.

nodes.label: Barrier: Keeper Device (Sufficiency Unknown)
nodes.detail: Keeper device installed but sufficiency under off-center displacement conditions unverified.

nodes.label: Barrier: Mechanical Block Absent (Documented)
nodes.detail: Blank field for mechanical block ID in LOTO record indicates failure to secure gravity load with independent restraint.

edges.rationale: Hydraulics bled (0 psi) removed primary support, leaving system reliant on unreliable wedged state.
edges.counterfactual: If hydraulics had not been bled or if a mechanical block existed, the gravity load would have been arrested.
edges.competingExplanation: Hydraulics were sufficient to hold position (contradicted by 0 psi gauge reading).
edges.evidenceGap: Engineering analysis of hydraulic bleed rate vs. structural integrity under zero pressure.

edges.rationale: Lack of inherent stop allowed beam to displace off-center when yoke moved, clearing the lifting point.
edges.counterfactual: If a mechanical stop existed on the carrier beam or yoke pocket, displacement would not have cleared the interference point.
edges.competingExplanation: Stop exists but was bypassed by operator error (unverified).
edges.evidenceGap: Mechanical design drawings for R3 stand.

edges.rationale: Off-center displacement subjected keeper to unverified loading conditions, potentially exceeding capacity.
edges.counterfactual: If the beam had not displaced off-center or if keeper rating exceeded displacement forces, fall would have been prevented.
edges.competingExplanation: Keeper failed due to fatigue/fracture unrelated to displacement (unverified).
edges.evidenceGap: Engineering analysis of Keeper rating vs. off-center displacement forces.

edges.rationale: Blank LOTO field indicates failure to secure gravity load with independent restraint per procedure expectations.
edges.counterfactual: If a mechanical block ID had been recorded and verified, the barrier would have existed independently of hydraulic pressure or wedging.
edges.competingExplanation: Block was physically present but undocumented (unverified).

edges.rationale: Reliance on unverified handwritten note instead of formal verification contributed to barrier failure.
edges.counterfactual: If a competent authority had verified and documented the keeper check before Turn 2 work, the event might have been prevented or detected earlier.

edges.rationale: Assuming wedging sufficed led to failure to install/verify mechanical block, leaving barrier dependent on unreliable condition.
edges.counterfactual: If a verified mechanical block had been installed and documented before bleeding hydraulics, the gravity load would have been arrested regardless of wedging loss.
edges.evidenceGap: Engineering analysis of Keeper rating vs. off-center displacement.

verificationFindings.issue: Causal edge from Design Gap (node-krlpg3) to Off-Center Displacement (node-1rdukjl). The rationale claims lack of stop allowed displacement. Evidence supports design gap but does not prove the specific mechanism caused off-center movement; could be operator error or external force.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Mechanical design drawings for R3 stand and witness testimony on how yoke moved downward to confirm if it was uncontrolled drift vs active command.
verificationFindings.question: Did an independent mechanical stop exist that would have prevented off-center displacement, and what evidence confirms the specific mechanism of movement?

verificationFindings.issue: Causal edge from Off-Center Displacement (node-1rdukjl) to Keeper Barrier Failure (node-1mcfvol). Rationale assumes keeper failed due to unverified loading. Evidence shows keeper present but does not prove it was overloaded or that displacement caused failure.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Engineering analysis of keeper rating vs off-center forces and inspection for deformation/fracture.
verificationFindings.question: Was the keeper device rated for the specific load path during off-center displacement, and is there evidence of structural damage?

verificationFindings.issue: Causal edge from Reliance on Wedging (node-xvnhzo) to Off-Center Displacement (node-1rdukjl). Rationale assumes assumption led to failure. Evidence does not prove the assumption caused displacement; could be independent event.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Timeline of hydraulic bleed vs yoke movement and witness accounts of any external forces.
verificationFindings.question: Did reliance on wedging directly cause or contribute to off-center displacement, or were these separate events?

verificationFindings.issue: Barrier node 'Reliance on Wedged State (Unverified)' lacks supporting evidence. Evidence shows hydraulics bled and no block documented but does not prove wedging was the only barrier relied upon.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Procedure requirements for gravity control after hydraulic isolation.
verificationFindings.question: What procedure or practice dictated reliance on wedging instead of a mechanical block?

verificationFindings.issue: Barrier node 'Keeper Device (Sufficiency Unknown)' lacks evidence of failure mode. Evidence shows keeper present but does not prove it failed due to overload.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Engineering analysis of load path during displacement.
verificationFindings.question: Did the keeper fail, or was another mechanism responsible for beam fall?
